mechanism: Apply the same-period EMA to weekly PRICE_HIGH and PRICE_LOW to form a dual-MA channel on W1. Daily close above the high-MA marks an overbought extreme (fade short); daily close below the low-MA marks an oversold extreme (fade long). Extremes are defined by price vs separate high/low envelopes rather than a mid-price band.
data_needed: iMA(Symbol, PERIOD_W1, MA_PERIOD, MODE_EMA, PRICE_HIGH) and PRICE_LOW; daily close; CopyBuffer series buffers.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD; higher TF W1 channel, lower TF D1 entries; MA_PERIOD default 12
why_new_for_mis: Separates high-feed and low-feed EMAs into an asymmetric extreme regime channel—MIS can tag overbought/oversold mean-reversion states from dual envelope breaches instead of single mid-line oscillators.
quote: One moving average is applied to the high price feed, while the other is applied to the low price feed. These two moving averages share the same period and, as a result, form a channel on the weekly time frame. When price levels break beyond this channel, we consider those price movements to generate the entry signals

mechanism: Build Target = Close/Open (then shift −HORIZON). Plot histogram of the ratio. A distribution tightly centered at 1 with narrow tails is read as evidence the market rarely trends and is mean-reverting; a wider off-center distribution would imply more frequent trending. Used as a pre-strategy market-character sensor before deploying mean-reversion entries.
data_needed: Historical OHLC CSV; Target=Close/Open; optional shift by HORIZON (10); histogram bins.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD daily bars; ~3000 bars fetched; train/test half-split; horizon 10 days
why_new_for_mis: Uses the shape of the Close/Open ratio distribution (center at 1, tail width) as an explicit mean-reversion vs trend regime diagnostic—MIS can gate strategy class by return-ratio density, not only volatility level.
quote: our target is centered around 1, with many observations being very close to 1. Additionally, the tail of this distribution is rather tight, except for a few outliers. This suggests that the market may not frequently trend. Otherwise, if the market did trend more frequently, we would've expected a wider distribution that is not centered around 1.

mechanism: On D1, compute EMA of open and EMA of close (same period). If open-MA < close-MA, bars tend to open low and close high → bullish tilt confirmation; if open-MA > close-MA → bearish tilt. Combined with the weekly channel break as a second-layer directional regime filter.
data_needed: iMA(..., PERIOD_D1, MA_PERIOD, MODE_EMA, PRICE_OPEN) and PRICE_CLOSE; latest buffer readings.
why_new_for_mis: Open-vs-close MA crossover as a soft intraday bias/tilt regime—MIS gets a candle-construction direction sensor distinct from high/low channel extremes.
quote: If the open moving average is beneath the close, then price levels are tending to open low and close high; this confirms our bullish entry signal. Otherwise, the opposite case confirms our bearish entry signal.

mechanism: Train sklearn models (LR/Ridge/Lasso/RF/GBR/LinearSVR) on OHLC to predict Close/Open shifted −10 days; pick LinearRegression after test RMSE (RF overfit). Export ONNX; MT5 OnnxRun on current D1 OHLC. Require model_outputs[0] > 1 to confirm long and < 1 to confirm short—statistical ensemble gate on top of technical extremes.
data_needed: OHLC features; Target=Close/Open.shift(-10); ONNX FloatTensor [1,4]→[1,1]; train 2011–2019, OOS 2020–2026.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1; forecast horizon 10 days; ONNX Linear Regressor embedded in EA
why_new_for_mis: Horizon forecast of the Close/Open ratio (not price level) as a binary confirmation sensor—MIS can fuse a lightweight ONNX ratio predictor with classical extreme tags for ensemble sensing.
quote: We will then seek additional confirmation from our statistical model and a pair of moving averages we applied to the daily time frame. … (model_outputs[0] > 1) … (model_outputs[0] < 1)

mechanism: stop_width = ATR(D1, ATR_PERIOD) × ATR_MULTIPLE + stops-level×point. Symmetric SL/TP and trailing use this width so position risk scales with current daily volatility; updates on each new D1 bar.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD D1 ATR period 14; ATR multiple 2
why_new_for_mis: Standard ATR-scaled risk envelope as a live volatility width sensor tied to mean-reversion entries—MIS can report vol-adaptive stop distance alongside extreme-channel state.
quote: we perform the final calculation of the stop-loss level that will be used for our symmetric stop-loss and take-profit system by using the current ATR reading.

mechanism: Fire only when three sensors concur on a new D1 bar: (1) daily close beyond weekly high/low EMA channel, (2) daily open-MA vs close-MA tilt aligns, (3) ONNX Close/Open forecast on the same side of 1. Long: close < low_ma AND open_ma < close_ma AND forecast > 1; short: close > high_ma AND open_ma > close_ma AND forecast < 1. Change event = confirmed extreme break with multi-layer assent.
data_needed: Weekly high/low MA buffers; daily open/close MA; ONNX model_outputs; daily close vector; new-bar stamp on LOWER_TIME_FRAME.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD W1+D1 ensemble; backtest 2020–2026 real ticks, random delay
why_new_for_mis: Explicit multi-sensor concurrence gate for mean-reversion change events—MIS can require channel extreme + open/close tilt + ratio forecast before tagging a fadeable regime breach.
quote: Our trading signal is registered first when the price breaks past the weekly moving average. We will then seek additional confirmation from our statistical model and a pair of moving averages we applied to the daily time frame.
